reason: Focused stop-order process to block registration where errors, fraud, or improper dealings must be prevented.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Stop orders prohibiting registration of instruments
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover issuing and registering stop orders, notice to owners, duration, and court review if withdrawal is refused.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when a stop order may block registration and how notice, duration, and court review work.

reason: Owner affidavit process to prevent registration in special circumstances and damages for wrongful affidavits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Affidavit preventing registration of an instrument
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections allow registration of an owner affidavit to block an instrument and create damages liability for wrongful, vexatious, or unsupported affidavits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how an owner affidavit can prevent registration and what liability may follow.

reason: Single rule for registering and removing a certificate of pending litigation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration and removal of certificate of pending litigation

evidenceText: A certificate of pending litigation in prescribed form may be registered
may be removed from registration by the registration of a court order or a certificate of the clerk

proposedGroups.reason: The text states how a certificate may be registered and when it may be removed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how a certificate of pending litigation is registered and removed.

reason: Registrar condition for registering instruments severing or consolidating registered land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration of instruments severing or consolidating registered land

evidenceText: not obliged to register an instrument severing or consolidating registered land
Community Planning Act have been complied with

proposedGroups.reason: The text makes registration depend on Community Planning Act compliance and necessary documentation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify what must satisfy the registrar before severing or consolidating registered land.

reason: Focused application workflow for registering a money judgment against registered land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application to register a memorial of judgment
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify who applies, joint-tenancy effect, acceptable name or land-description differences, multi-parcel applications, judgment copy attachment, and registration when in order.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how a judgment creditor applies to register a money judgment against registered land.

reason: Single binding-effect rule for a registered judgment while it remains in force.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effect of registered memorial of judgment

evidenceText: While a judgment is registered and remains in force it binds the interest of the judgment debtor

proposedGroups.reason: The text ties the registered judgment to the judgment debtor owner interest under the Enforcement of Money Judgments Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State what interest a registered judgment binds while it remains in force.

reason: Focused joint-tenancy rule for registered judgments after death before severance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registered judgment against joint tenant interests after death
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections contrast death of the judgment-debtor joint tenant with death of the other joint tenant and the resulting binding effect.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Distinguish how a registered judgment binds joint tenancy interests after a joint tenant dies.

reason: Single notice duty after a judgment is registered against registered land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice to owner after judgment registration

evidenceText: Upon the registration of a judgment against registered land
give notice of such registration to the owner

proposedGroups.reason: The text requires immediate notice to the owner of the affected interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State who must receive notice when a judgment is registered against registered land.

reason: The section separates notice and expiry or extension of judgment registration from assignment of a registered judgment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice to judgment creditor and expiry or extension of registration
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover notice requests, affidavit grounds, notice to the creditor, ninety-day cessation, court extension, and further extension.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how notice to a judgment creditor can lead to cessation or extension of registration.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assignment of a registered judgment
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow assignment registration and pass the assignor interest, rights, powers, privileges, and limitations to the assignee.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how a registered judgment may be assigned and what passes to the assignee.

reason: Single prescribed-form method for withdrawing or removing a registered judgment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Withdrawing or removing a memorial of judgment

evidenceText: A registered judgment may be withdrawn or removed from registration
by an instrument in prescribed form

proposedGroups.reason: The text states how a registered judgment may be withdrawn or removed in whole, in part, or as to affected land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how a registered judgment may be withdrawn or removed from registration.

reason: Damages action for improper judgment registration and deemed wrongful registration where debtor-owner matching was not reasonably checked.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Damages against judgment creditor for improper registration
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections create a cause of action and deem registration wrongful if reasonable steps were not taken to match debtor and owner.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when damages may be claimed against a judgment creditor for improper registration.

reason: Conflict rule giving the Land Titles Act judgment provisions priority over conflicting Enforcement of Money Judgments Act provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Paramountcy of Land Titles Act judgment provisions

evidenceText: the provisions of this Act apply

proposedGroups.reason: The text states which provisions prevail in a conflict.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State which Act applies when judgment registration provisions conflict.

reason: Focused filing and registration rule for powers of attorney and instruments executed under them.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration or filing of powers of attorney
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover registration or filing, registrar recognition, proof by statutory declaration, and electronic-instrument exceptions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how powers of attorney are filed or registered and used to prove execution.

reason: The section separates registration and notice effect of conditions or covenants from limits and discharge.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration and notice effect of land conditions or covenants
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow registration and bind successive owners with notice if the condition or covenant runs with land, subject to court modification or discharge grounds.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how registering a condition or covenant affects successive owners.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Limits and discharge of registered conditions or covenants
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections clarify registration does not determine whether a covenant runs with land or is enforceable and allow discharge by registered instrument.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the limits of registration and how conditions or covenants may be discharged.

reason: Focused numbering and later-transfer rule for conditions and covenants in transfers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Numbered conditions and covenants in transfers
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover Registrar General numbering, owner designation of numbers in transfers, and no need to repeat conditions or covenants later.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how numbered conditions or covenants are used in transfers.

reason: Registrar duty to receive expropriation instruments and power to request further documentation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Instrument evidencing expropriation of registered land

evidenceText: shall receive instruments evidencing an expropriation of registered land

proposedGroups.reason: The text addresses expropriation instruments under Canadian or provincial enactments and documentation needed to carry out the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how the registrar handles instruments evidencing expropriation.

reason: Cohesive bankruptcy registration workflow and notice-based correction if the bankrupt is not the owner.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Bankruptcy proceedings affecting registered land
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover trustee registration, notices, owner requests, affidavit grounds, thirty-day cessation, court confirmation, and ownership restoration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how bankruptcy orders or assignments are registered and corrected if the bankrupt is not the owner.

reason: Focused tax sale workflow for certificates, redemption notices, cancellation, and purchaser title registration.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Tax sale proceedings for registered land
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address certificate registration, redemption notice and cancellation, and registration of purchaser title without inquiry into irregularities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how tax sale certificates, redemptions, and purchaser title registration work.
